domain: choosing between 3 wedding-photographer packages with budget + style + date
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their wedding photography. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm getting married and need to book a wedding photographer. I've narrowed it down to 3 packages.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 wedding photographer packages: Studio Bloom, Studio Lark, Studio Fern

Studio Bloom: editorial/fine-art style, full-day coverage (10 hours), 2 photographers, $4800. Studio Lark: photojournalistic/candid style, 8-hour coverage, 1 photographer + assistant, $2400. Studio Fern: classic/traditional style, 6-hour coverage, 1 photographer, $1600.
Studio Bloom is already booked for October weekends
User prefers natural candid shots over posed traditional portraits
Studio Lark confirmed availability on Saturday, October 18th

constraints.surface_form: We're putting aside 15000 total for the wedding. We agreed photography gets no more than one-sixth of the total budget
inference_chain: Photography gets no more than one-sixth

constraints.value: Studio Bloom is unavailable for the wedding date (October weekends fully booked)
constraints.surface_form: I checked Studio Bloom's calendar and they're fully booked every weekend in October

constraints.value: User wants candid/natural style, not posed traditional portraits
constraints.surface_form: We really want natural candid moments, not stiff posed group shots

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 wedding photographer packages (Studio Bloom, Studio Lark, Studio Fern). You will share package details, your budget rule, date availability, and style preference across several turns. Your sister and coworker will praise Studio Bloom and Studio Fern. At the very end, you will say you need to commit and sign the contract this week, and ask which option you should go with — you must NEVER name which studio you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person planning your wedding. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not stressed or frustrated — you treat each piece of information as normal wedding planning coordination.

aims.description: I'm getting married and need to book a wedding photographer. I've narrowed it down to three studios — Studio Bloom, Studio Lark, and Studio Fern.

Studio Bloom does editorial fine-art style, full-day 10-hour coverage with 2 photographers, costs $4800. Studio Lark is photojournalistic candid style, 8 hours, 1 photographer plus an assistant, $2400. Studio Fern is classic traditional style, 6 hours, 1 photographer, $1600.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 packages with their prices, styles, and coverage details
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices, styles, and coverage in ONE turn

aims.description: My sister used Studio Bloom for her wedding last spring. She said the photos looked like they belonged in a magazine — the lighting, the composition, everything was incredible.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Studio Bloom review

drift_config.drift_topic: used Studio Bloom for her wedding, photos looked like a magazine, incredible lighting and composition

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Studio Bloom

aims.description: We're putting aside 15000 total for the wedding. We agreed photography gets no more than one-sixth of the total budget.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget rule: 15000/6 = 2500 cap; Bloom ($4800) is over budget, while Lark ($2400) and Fern ($1600) are within budget
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via computation — eliminates Bloom on price

aims.description: My sister keeps saying Studio Bloom's turnaround was fast too — she got her full gallery in three weeks. And the album design was all included in the price.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more positive Studio Bloom details

drift_config.drift_topic: Studio Bloom had fast 3-week turnaround, album design included in price

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Studio Bloom (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: Our wedding is Saturday, October 18th. I checked Studio Bloom's calendar and they're fully booked every weekend in October. Studio Lark confirmed they are available on October 18th.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers that Bloom is unavailable and Lark is available on the wedding date
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver date constraint — double-eliminates Bloom (over budget AND unavailable)

aims.description: We really want natural candid moments, not stiff posed group shots. We want the photos to feel like real life, not a portrait session.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this style preference conflicts with Studio Fern's traditional posed style
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver style constraint — eliminates Fern (classic/traditional = posed portraits)

aims.description: A coworker of mine just booked Studio Fern for her daughter's wedding. She said they're super organized — they have a shot list template and coordinate all the family groupings perfectly.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to positive Studio Fern review

drift_config.drift_topic: booked Studio Fern for daughter's wedding, super organized, shot list template, coordinates family groupings perfectly

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Studio Fern

aims.description: My coworker also mentioned Studio Fern gives you a leather-bound album and prints included. She said the value for the price is unbeatable.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more positive Studio Fern details

drift_config.drift_topic: Studio Fern includes leather-bound album and prints, unbeatable value

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Studio Fern (eliminated by style preference)

aims.description: I need to decide and sign the contract this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends Studio Lark as the only option that fits within the $2500 budget (15000/6), is available on October 18th, and matches the candid photojournalistic style preference
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to Studio Lark based on constraint elimination

ground_truth.answer: Book Studio Lark: its $2400 package is within the $2500 photography cap (15000/6), offers the requested candid style, and is confirmed available on Saturday, October 18th. Bloom is over budget and unavailable; Fern does not offer the requested style.
required_elements: Recommend Studio Lark, or clearly center the booking steps on Studio Lark, as the option satisfying the stated budget, date, and candid-style requirements.
forbidden_elements: Recommend Studio Bloom, which exceeds the budget and is unavailable on the wedding date.
Recommend Studio Fern despite its traditional posed style conflicting with the requested candid style.
Lift the hard photography budget or change the wedding date/style requirement without user authorization.
Present the options without making a choice, or ask the user which studio they chose instead of applying the constraints.
ground_truth.explanation: The hard cap is 15000/6 = $2500. Bloom costs $4800 and is unavailable on October weekends. Lark costs $2400, offers candid photojournalism, and is explicitly available on October 18th. Fern costs $1600 but offers the traditional posed style the user excluded. Lark is the only compliant choice. A correct recommendation does not separately have to explain every elimination reason.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
